PROSECUTION WITNESSES 5.
Prosecution examined HC Chhaju Ram as PW1.

His version is reproduced as under:-
"
In complaint case No. 38998/2018, accused Yog Maya was declared as P.O.

As the concerned Court had ordered an FIR to be registered against the accused Yog Maya under Section 174-A, therefore, I prepared a tehrir which is Ex.PW-1/A bearing my signature at point A and got the FIR No. 376/22 dated 08.07.2022 registered on the same.

Thereafter, I searched for the accused and for her search I went to address i.e.
RZ-2/230, J Block, Dayalpur, Sagarpur but the accused was not found there.

I recorded the statement of one person Sanjeev Kumar Walia, Vicky Gupta and Rohit,
who were residing at the 3 rd floor, upper ground floor and 3rd floor respectively of the above mentioned address and recorded their statements which is Ex.PW-1/B,
Ex.PW-1/C and Ex.PW-1/D respectively, all bearing my signature at point A.

When the accused was not found at the above mentioned address, I obtained other address of the accused from the cheque details of the accused from the case file of case No.
38998/2018.
Thereafter, I obtained the address of the accused from the concerned bank namely SBI.

On obtaining the address from the bank, I reached HARJOT SINGH SINGH Date:

2 2025.05.30 17:06:44 +0545 at the address i.e. RZ-J-11A/230, West Sagarpur, New Delhi-110046, where I met with the owner of the said address Ravinder Gupta and I recorded his statement which is Ex.PW-1/E bearing my signature at point A, who informed me that the accused was staying at the above address 20 years back and she has vacated the said premises.
I also recorded statement of Sarita Kataria wife of Late Sh. Rohtash Kataria, who was the complainant in the above mentioned complaint case, which is Ex.PW-1/F bearing my signature at point A.

Thereafter, on the information of the secret informer, I got the address of the accused and reached at the address i.e. RZ-5/230, Dayal Park, West Sagarpur, and found the accused at the above said address.
The accused informed me that my husband is not at home and therefore I would come to PS Janakpuri alongwith him.
On the same day, she came to the PS and I arrested her in complaint case and released her on bail at the same time.

I also served notice under Section 41.A Cr.PC in the present case Ex.PW-1/G bearing my signature at point A. I also recorded disclosure statement of the accused at the PS itself which is Ex.PW-1/H bearing my signature at point A."
Accused was correctly identified by the witness.
6. Prosecution examined Sh. Jitender Jakhar as PW2.

His version is reproduced as under:-
"I have been summoned by this Court to produce the original case file of complaint case No. 38998/2018.
I produce the original case file.
Witness has shown the original order dated 30.03.2022, the copy of same is now Ex.PW-2/A (OSR), wherein the accused was declared PO on 30.03.2022."
7. Prosecution examined W/HC Nisha as PW3.

Her version is reproduced as under:-
"On 06.04.2023, I was present at the PS Janakpuri and on that day, the accused Yog Maya had come to the PS alongwith her husband.
IO informed about the present case against her.

On conducting her interrogation in my HARJOT SINGH SINGH Date:
2025.05.30 17:06:58 +0545 presence, accused told the IO HC Chhaju Ram that she used to reside at RZJ11A/233 J Block, West Sagarpur Delhi long time back and had made identity cards on that address itself.
She further stated that presently she resides on rent at RZ5/230 Dayal Park, West Sagarpur Delhi (Amit Bansal is the owner).
She further stated that account no.32900762356 SBI Branch C Block Janakpuri belongs to her.
She did not appear in Court no.213 Dwarka Delhi in CC no.38998/2018 on several occasions.
IO recorded her disclosure statement in my presence which is already Ex.PW1/H bearing my signature at point B.
Accused was taken for medical examination and thereafter, she was produced in Court no.211 where she was granted bail."
Accused was correctly identified by the witness.
8. Prosecution examined Ms. Priyanka Rawat as PW4.

Hence the above documents were ordered to be read in evidence without their formal proof.
STATEMENT OF THE ACCUSED AND DEFENCE EVIDENCE 10.

Thereafter, before the start of defence evidence in order to allow the accused person to personally explain the incriminating circumstances appearing in evidence against her, the statement of the accused person was recorded on 08.01.2025 without oath under section 351 BNSS, wherein she has stated that HARJOT by HARJOT SINGH SINGH Date: 2025.05.30 17:07:10 +0545 she is innocent and has falsely been implicated in the present case.
She further stated that she did not want to lead defence evidence.
FINAL ARGUMENTS 11.
I have heard the Ld. APP for the State and Ld. LAC for the accused at length.
I have also given my thoughtful consideration to the material appearing on record.
12. It is argued by the Ld. APP for the State that all the ingredients of the offence are fulfilled in the present case.
He has argued that prosecution witnesses have categorically deposed about the commission of offence and there is no ground to disbelieve their testimony.
He further contends that the documentary evidence has proved the offence beyond reasonable doubt.
As such, it is prayed that the accused be punished for the said offence.
13. Per contra, the Ld. LAC for the accused has argued that the State has failed to establish its case beyond reasonable doubt.

The Ld. LAC further argued that the entire case of the prosecution is false and fabricated and the same is evident from the material inconsistencies and contradictions borne out from the material on record.
It is argued that the prosecution has failed to discharge the burden cast upon it.
As such, it is prayed that the accused be acquitted for the said offence.

INGREDIENTS OF THE OFFENCE 14. Brief, outline of offence for which the accused has been tried is, section 174A IPC which describes as under:-
174A. Non-appearance in response to a proclamation under section 82 of Act 2 of 1974.--
State vs Yog Maya on 30 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159095840/
4

Whoever fails to appear at the specified place and the specified time as HARJOT SINGH SINGH Date:
2025.05.30 17:07:23 +0545 required by a proclamation published under sub-section (1) of section 82 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years or with fine or with both,
and where a declaration has been made under sub section (4) of that section pronouncing him as a proclaimed offender, he shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to seven years and shall also be liable to fine.

15. The essential ingredients for conviction u/s 174A IPC are as follows:-
(a) Proclamation u/s 82 CrPC: A proclamation must have been issued by a court declaring a person as a absconder for not appearing despite the issuance of warrants (b) Failure to appear: The person knowingly fails to appear at the time and place specified in the proclamation issued against him (c) Knowledge of the proclamation: It must be shown that the accused had knowledge of the proclamation issued against him.
APPRECIATION OF EVIDENCE 16.
In the present case, it is not disputed that a proclamation has been issued by the court declaring the accused Yog Maya as absconder.
Order passed by Ld. MM, NI Act-05, South West District, dated 30.03.2022, Ex. PW 2/A is part of judicial record.
However, it remained not proved that the accused Yog Maya knowingly fails to appear before the court or she had the knowledge regarding the proclamation issued against her.

The basis of the observation is discussed as follows:-
17.
The accused was declared absconder on the basis of the statement of the process server HC Chander Shekhar.

As per the statement of the process server dated 30.03.2022, he received the process u/s 82 CrPC against accused Yog Maya W/o Sh. Prem Pal Gupta, R/o RZ-2/230, J Block,
Dayal Park, Sagarpur HARJOT SINGH SINGH Date:
2025.05.30 17:08:09 +0545 West, New Delhi-46.
The process server visited the address where the accused was not found.
Further, one person namely, Ashok Kumar S/o Sardari Lal met the process server at the address and it was told by him that accused Yog Maya never ever resided at the given address.

18. Further, during investigation HC Chhaju Ram went to the address i.e. R/o RZ-J-11A/230, West Sagarpur, New Delhi-46 and met with one Mr. Ravinder Gupta and it was stated by him that the accused stayed at the given address 20 years back and has vacated the premises.

Further, HC Chhaju Ram visited the address i.e. RZ-2/230, J Block, Dayal Park, Sagarpur West, New Delhi-46 and he met Sanjeev Kumar Walia, Vicky Gupta and Rohit and their statements were recorded Ex. PW 1/B,
State vs Yog Maya on 30 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159095840/
5 Ex. PW 1/C and Ex. PW 1/D respectively.

As per their statements, accused Yog Maya never resided at the address i.e. RZ-2/230, J Block, Dayal Park, Sagarpur West, New Delhi-46 (address mentioned on the proclamation).
19.

Therefore, it remained not established that the accused Yog Maya ever resided at the address i.e.
RZ-2/230, J Block, Dayal Park, Sagarpur West, New Delhi-46 and thus had the knowledge of the proclamation issued against her or that she knowingly fails to appear before the court.
Further, the proclamation was not published in any newspaper.
Therefore, essential ingredients of the offence remained not proved.
CONCLUSION 20.
From the above discussion, and the surrounding circumstances, the essential ingredients of the offence remained not proved as discussed above.
In the present case, several reasonable doubts have emerged in the narrative put forth by prosecution as analyzed hereinabove.

The basic ingredient of Section 174A IPC has not been proved and the inescapable conclusion is that the HARJOT by HARJOT SINGH SINGH Date: 2025.05.30 17:08:26 +0545 accused is entitled to benefit of doubt.
Accused Yog Maya is thus, acquitted of the offences u/s 174A IPC Announced in the open Court HARJOT by HARJOT on 30.05.2025 in the presence SINGH SINGH Date: 2025.05.30 17:08:33 +0545 of the accused.
